paragraphs: Mah shettiqqenu chakamenu za"l qaddishim beshacharit inyanam hu kak dehattepilla hi letzorek tiqqun veilluy olamot atzilut, beria, yetzira, asiyya, vehu ki min hatchalat hattepilla ad baruk sheamar hu baolam haasiyya, umishsham ad yotzer or beolam hayyetzira, umishsham ad tepillat shemoneh esreh beolam habberia, utepillat shemoneh esreh hi baatzilut, veachar kak yoredim meilla letatta, lepi shebbime hachol en banu koach lehaamidam beilluy hannaaseh lahem ella raq lepi shaa vetekep chozerim limqoman, vehinneh min ashre ad tepilla ledavid bibria, umishsham ad en qadosh koAdonai bitzira, umishsham ad alenu leshabbeach baasiyya, velaken tiqqenu qaddish ben kol olam veolam deal yede haqqaddish hamtuqqan al pi hassod bemispar hattebot vehaotiyyot shebbo tihyeh shelemot aliyyat haolamot lemala mimmadregatam velazeh bau kol tebotayv veken hachamishsha ummanim harishonim shebbo kemispar yadua umekuvvan letzorek aliyyat haolamot ulekak nitqan haqqaddish bilshon targum kede shello yaalu haqqelippot gam ken baaliyyat haolamot lehitachez bahem velinoq shepa mehem leet atta vehu ki hem makkirim umebinim leshon hattargum vekaasher shomein hashshebach haggadol vehannora vehaqqadosh hazzeh shel haqqaddish hem niknaim veen olim vegam od al yede kavvanatenu beqaddish yistalleq hannitzotz shel haqqedushsha shehu hachayyut shebbetok haqqelippot veyaaleh lemala veyitchabber im haqqedushsha ubazeh yihyeh haknaa gedola meod lehaqqelippot veyitparedu kol poale aven velaken ameru bazzohar haqqadosh al haqqaddish deihu mittebar shelleshelleayyen deparzela vekannizkar kol zeh beseper hakkavvanot lerabbenu haari"y za"l ubeseper "pardes" lerashi"y za"l siman v' natan taam acher mah shennitqan betargum vehaiqqar taam haari"y za"l umah shello omerim qaddish qodem tepillat shemoneh esreh nebaer leqamman beezrat hashshem:

clarification.explanation:
What our sages instituted as the Kaddishes of Shacharit - their meaning, according to the secret: prayer rectifies and elevates the worlds of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah. From the start of the prayer until 'Baruch She'amar' - in the world of Asiyah; from there until 'Yotzer Or' - in Yetzirah; from there until the Amidah - in Beriah; and the Amidah - in Atzilut; and afterward one descends from above to below, since on weekdays we lack the strength to sustain the worlds in elevation except momentarily, and they immediately return to their place (from 'Ashrei' until 'Tefillah LeDavid' [Psalm 86] in Beriah, until 'Ein Kadosh KaHashem' in Yetzirah, until 'Aleinu LeShabeach' in Asiyah). Therefore they instituted a Kaddish between one world and the next, so that through the Kaddish - constructed according to the secret in the number of its words and letters (and likewise the first five 'craftsmen' phrases within it) - the ascent of the worlds above their level is completed.
And they instituted the Kaddish in the language of Targum (Aramaic), so that the klipot too should not ascend in the worlds' ascent to attach themselves and draw from them - for they understand the Aramaic language, and when they hear this great and awesome praise they become subdued and do not ascend; furthermore, through our intention in the Kaddish, the spark of holiness (the vitality) within the klipot departs and ascends to join with holiness, and this is a great subduing of the klipot. Therefore it is said in the Zohar concerning the Kaddish that it 'breaks iron chains.' All this is from the Sefer HaKavanot of the Arizal, of blessed memory; and the reason Kaddish is not said before the Amidah will be explained elsewhere.
takeaways: Prayer elevates the four worlds (Asiyah, Yetzirah, Beriah, Atzilut), and the Kaddish between one world and the next - constructed according to the number of its words - completes their ascent.

The Kaddish is in Aramaic so that the klipot (which understand Targum) become subdued and do not ascend with the worlds; and through the intention of the Kaddish the spark of holiness within the klipot ascends - hence it 'breaks iron chains.'

paragraphs: Min yehe shemeh rabba mebarak ad bealema tzarik lihyot k"ch tebot al pi hassod veim neemar mikkol birketa en kan ella k"z tebot ulekak katab rabbenu harasha"sh za"l shetztzarik lomar min kol lehashlim k"ch vaasher piqpeq rabbenu morenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l behaggahato beshaar hakkavvanot al amirat min kol hinneh besipre haq' rab pealim taanti teanot gedolot al debarayv vesham hebeti pasuq "vibareku sham kebodeka umeromam al kol beraka utehilla" (nechemya t, h) ulepi dibre rabbenu morenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l haya tzarik lomar kan mikkol gam sham hebeti dimyon laamirat min kol bammiqra bedaniyyel ' "uberie basar min kol hayladim" (pasuq tv), vegam ballasho targum nimtza sham besiman b' "bechakema di itay bi min kol chayyayya" (pasuq l), veken besiman z' "di tishne min kol malkuyyota" (pasuq kg):

clarification.explanation: From 'Yehei Shmei Rabba Mevarach' until 'Be'alma' there must be, according to the secret, twenty-eight words; and if one says only 'Mikol Birchata' there are only twenty-seven. Therefore one must say 'Min Kol Birchata' to complete the twenty-eight, as the Rashash wrote (and this is also proven from the wording of verses and from the Aramaic of the Book of Daniel).
takeaways: In the Kaddish one says 'Min Kol Birchata' (not 'Mikol') in order to complete the count of twenty-eight words, which carries a secret meaning.

paragraphs: Mitzvat aniyyat haqqaddish shel "yehe shemeh rabba mebarak" hu sheyyishma haoneh techillat haqqaddish shehu b' tebot "yitgaddal veyitqaddash", ki "yehe shemeh rabba mebarak" hu aniyya al "yitgaddel", lekak lekattechilla yasimu kol hatztzibbur libbam lishmoa kol haqqaddish min tebat yitgaddel kede lekavven al ma hem onin, mihu yachid shenniknas lebet hakkeneset, o, shessiyyem tepillat shemoneh esreh umatza hatztzibbur onin qaddish yaaneh immahem, veraq baamirat amen deqodem "yehe shemeh rabba" ikka pelugta deyesh omerim sheyyatchil laanot min "yehe shemeh rabba mebarak" velo yomar amen dachashib amen yetoma, veyesh omerim sheyyukal laanot amen gam ken vela have amen yetoma ubesipri haq' "mqbtzyl" haaleti man daabad kemar abad uman daabad kemar abad, dehaonin amen yesh lahem semika lismok veken rauy lehorot:

clarification.explanation: The mitzvah of answering the Kaddish ('Yehei Shmei Rabba Mevarach') requires that the one answering hear the beginning of the Kaddish, the two words 'Yitgadal VeYitkadash,' since 'Yehei Shmei Rabba Mevarach' is the response to 'Yitgadal'; therefore, ideally, the whole congregation should pay attention to hear the Kaddish from 'Yitgadal,' in order to have intention for what they are answering. Nevertheless, an individual who enters the synagogue [late], or who finished the Amidah and found the congregation answering Kaddish, may answer with them. And only regarding the 'Amen' that precedes 'Yehei Shmei Rabba' is there a dispute: some say one should begin answering from 'Yehei Shmei Rabba Mevarach' and not say that 'Amen' (which is considered an 'orphaned Amen'), and some say one may also answer 'Amen,' and it is not an orphaned Amen. The Ben Ish Chai (in Makbetziel) concluded that whoever acts either way has grounds to rely upon, and those who answer 'Amen' have support, and so it is fitting to instruct.
takeaways: The mitzvah of answering Kaddish is to hear from 'Yitgadal VeYitkadash' and have intention; 'Yehei Shmei Rabba' is the response to 'Yitgadal.'

One who enters in the middle and finds the congregation answering may answer with them; regarding the 'Amen' preceding 'Yehei Shmei Rabba' there is a dispute, but in practice one who answers 'Amen' has grounds to rely upon.

paragraphs: Im hitchil lomar qaddish baasara veyatzeu miqtzatan gomerin oto haqqaddish, vehu shennishtayyer rubban abal im lo nishtayyer rubban lo, uben hake uben hake otam sheyyatzeu alehem neemar "veozebe Adonai yakelu" (yeshaya , kch), veim nishar asara let lan bah, veim hayu asara baamirat parashat hattamid vehaqqarebbanot ubarayta derabbi yishmael veyatzeu mehem lo yukal lomar qaddish im lo yesh asara, veken hu haddin im hayu asara bizmirot veshirat hayyam veyatzeu mehem qodem sheyyatchil haqqaddish lo yomar qaddish bepachot measara, veken hu haddin im hayu asara baamirat ashre deqodem mincha veyatzeu miqtzatan qodem shehitchil haqqaddish lo yomar bepachot measara ap al pi deqaddishim ellu choba hen, vekannizkar hattaam beshulchan aruk lerabbenu zalman za"l siman n"ch seip d':

clarification.explanation: If they began saying Kaddish with a quorum of ten and part of them left - they finish the Kaddish if a majority remains (though those who left deserve reproach, 'and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed'); if the majority does not remain, they do not finish it. Likewise, if there was a quorum during the recitation of the sacrifices/the passage of the daily offering/Zemirot/Ashrei before Minchah, and they left before the Kaddish itself began - one may not say Kaddish with fewer than ten, even though these Kaddishes are obligatory.
takeaways: A Kaddish that began with ten and the quorum diminished - they continue if a majority remains.
If the quorum broke before the Kaddish itself began - it is not said with fewer than ten.

paragraphs: Im hem asara betzimtzum veechad mehem mitpallel tepillat shemoneh esreh sheeno yakol laanot immahem qaddish ap al pi ken mitztarep immahem, vehu haddin apillu im hayu shenayim o shelosha o arbaa mitpallelin kol shennishar rob sheonin qaddish veammanim muttar lomar qaddish, dekol sheyyesh sham asara shekina shora alehem vikolim lomar dabar shebbiqdushsha, mah sheen ken bachazara shane vekaasher nebaer qamman beezrat hashshem, mihu im haya echad mehaasara yashen yesh omerim dibechad bilbad shave yashen yekolim lomar qaddish abal bishnayim lo deen kebod shamayim letzarep shenayim yeshenim, veyesh omerim sheen ledammot yashen lemitpallel lepi shehayyashen yesh bo histallequt neshama qetzat veen qedushsha shora alayv ella adderabba qetzat tuma shora alayv apillu yashan bayyom, laken en letzarep apillu beechad veken rauy lehorot daapillu beechad yashan lo yomru qaddish ella ad sheyyaqitzu oto, veim i epshar lahaqitzo lo yomru:

clarification.explanation: If there were exactly ten and one of them is praying the Amidah and cannot answer Kaddish - he nevertheless counts toward the quorum; the same applies even if two, three, or four are praying, so long as a majority who answer Kaddish and Amens remains, it is permitted to say Kaddish, since wherever there are ten the Divine Presence rests and they may say a matter of holiness (unlike the chazan's repetition, as will be explained). But if one of the ten is asleep - some say a single sleeping person may be counted, but not two (since it is not respectful of Heaven to count two sleeping men); and some say one should not compare a sleeping person to one who is praying, since a sleeper has a certain withdrawal of the soul and holiness does not rest upon him, but rather a degree of impurity (even sleeping by day), and therefore not even one may be counted. And so it is fitting to instruct: even with one asleep, they should not say Kaddish until they wake him, and if it is impossible to wake him, they should not say it.
takeaways: Ten present in exact number, with one (or several) praying the Amidah - they count toward Kaddish, so long as a majority who can answer remains.
A person asleep in the quorum - in practice is not counted (since there is a withdrawal of the soul); wake him, and if that is not possible, do not say Kaddish.

paragraphs: Cheresh hamdabber veeno shomea, o shomea veeno medabber hare ken kepiqchim umitztarepim lekol dabar shebbiqdushsha ap al pi sheen onin immahem, vaapillu im yesh shalosh vearba meellu kol sheyyesh rob onim mitztarepim, chutz min hachazara shel tepillat shemoneh esreh debaenan tisha shomein chazarat sh"tz veonin amen vekaasher yitbaer leqamman, abal mi sheeno shomea velo medabber hare hu keshoteh veqatan deeno mitztarep vezeh cheresh sheddibberu bo chakamim bekol maqom, veken menuddeh veonen en mitztarepim lekol dabar shebbiqdushsha, abal abaryan sheabar al gezerat tzibbur sheggazeru becherem meachar shello nidduhu beperush metzarep, vehashshikkor im eno yakol ledabber bipne hammelek eno mitztarep:

clarification.explanation: A deaf-mute who speaks but does not hear, or hears but does not speak, counts toward the quorum for a matter of holiness (even though he does not actually answer), so long as a majority of those present answer; but for the chazan's repetition, nine who hear and answer Amen are required. One who neither hears nor speaks is like an imbecile or a minor and does not count. One under a ban and a mourner before burial do not count; a transgressor who was not explicitly excommunicated does count; a drunkard who cannot speak coherently before a king does not count.
takeaways: A deaf-mute (who hears or speaks, not both) counts toward an ordinary quorum, but not toward the chazan's repetition.
One under a ban, a mourner before burial, and a severely intoxicated person do not count toward the quorum.

paragraphs: Tzarik sheyyihyu kol haasara bemaqom echad ushelicha tzibbur shehu mikkelalam gam ken hu immahem, abal miqtzatam becheder zeh umiqtzatam becheder zeh enam mitztarepim ap al pi sheppetach patucha benehem, veteba o bima shebbebet hakkeneset sheomed aleha hashlicha tzibbur ap al pi shehi gabohha asara tepachim urechaba harbeh veyesh lah mechitztzot gebohim asara, vehashshalicha tzibbur mitztarep immahem umotziam yede choba, mippene ki hatteba hazzot betela legabbe bet hakkeneset daasuya letzorek bet hakkeneset hi, veha debaenan sheyyihyu kol haasara bemaqom echad kol zeh leinyan tzerup, abal im yesh asara bemaqom echad sheomerim qaddish o qedushsha kol hashshomea qolam apillu omed bebayit acher vaapillu yesh beno lebenam kamma battim hare zeh oneh immahem qaddish, veraq shello yihyeh mapsiq beno lebenam tinnup o akku"m, veha deamarnu detinnup o akku"m mapsiq veeno oneh haynu im zeh omed bebayit acher sheddino hu sheeno mitztarep immahem, abal im omed bemaqom echad apillu sheyyesh beoto maqom akku"m echad omed sham hare zeh oneh im hatztzibbur qaddish uqedushsha vekol dabar shebbiqdushsha, vetzarik lehazhir haam bezeh haddabar shettamid yimmatze akku"m omedim bepetach bet hakkeneset limkor sham ezeh dabar ubene adam holekim bammaboy chutz lappetach achar haakku"m veshomeim qaddish vekayyotze deen laanot, veraq im niknas haakku"m betok bet hakkeneset lo ikpat lan bazeh vekol hatztzibbur shehem betok bet hakkeneset onim kol dabar shebbiqdushsha apillu otam haomedim achare haakku"m:

clarification.explanation: All ten (including the chazan) must be in the very same place; if some are in a different room, they do not combine even if there is an open door between them. The platform in the synagogue is considered nullified in relation to the synagogue and does not constitute a separation. One who hears the sound of Kaddish/Kedushah from another house may answer along with them (provided there is no interruption of filth or a gentile standing in between - but if he is in the same place as the congregation, even if a gentile is present there, he does answer). And the people must be warned about this: sometimes gentiles stand at the entrance of the synagogue to sell something, and one who stands in the alley outside the entrance - behind the gentile - and hears Kaddish, does not answer. But if the gentile enters into the synagogue itself, the entire congregation inside answers, even those standing behind him.
takeaways: The quorum must be in the very same place; but one who hears from another house may answer (provided there is no interruption of filth/a gentile in between).
A gentile standing at the entrance of the synagogue interrupts for one standing outside; once the gentile enters inside, everyone answers.

paragraphs: Qaddish shettapesu meummad kegon qaddish sheachar haamida, veachar hahallel, shehaya omed bitchillato yishshaer omed ad achar aniyyat "amen yehe shemeh rabba" kullah, veken yesh lizzaher bekol haqqaddishim shemmizdammen shehu haya yosheb keshehitchilu beqaddish veabar zaqen o talmid chakam veqam mippenehem sheyyishshaer omed ad achar aniyyat "amen yehe shemeh rabba", meachar shekkebar amad chashib tepaso meummad:

clarification.explanation: A Kaddish in which one was standing from the outset (such as after the Amidah or after Hallel) - one remains standing until the end of the response 'Amen Yehei Shmei Rabba.' Likewise, one who was sitting and rose out of respect for an elder or Torah scholar in the middle of the Kaddish is considered as one whom the Kaddish 'caught standing,' and remains standing until the end.
takeaways: A Kaddish that began while standing (or during which one rose) - one remains standing until the end of 'Amen Yehei Shmei Rabba.'

paragraphs: Keshem shetztzarik lehizzaher mibberaka sheenah tzerika kak yizzaher shello leharbot baqqaddishim, mihu im lamad tora shebbiktab verotzeh lomar qaddish yehe shelama, veachar kak lamad tora shebbeal peh veomer qaddish al yisrael o lehepek let lan bah sheen bazeh marbeh baqqaddishim, ulekak nohagim poh ayarenu lomar kol yom achar qebiut tora shebbeal peh qaddish al yisrael veachar kak lomedim tehillim veomerim qaddish yehe shelama, veken osim belel chag hashshabuot vehoshana rabba, veshamati sheggam beir haqqodesh minhagam lomar bishte lelot hannizkarim qaddish achar tora shebbiktab, veqaddish achar tora shebbeal peh:

clarification.explanation: Just as one is careful about an unnecessary blessing, so one is careful about multiplying Kaddishes; but a Kaddish after studying the Written Torah and then after studying the Oral Torah (or vice versa) is not considered multiplication, and so the custom developed of saying the Kaddish 'Al Yisrael' after Oral Torah study, and afterward studying Tehillim and saying 'Yehei Shlama' (and likewise on the night of Shavuot and Hoshana Rabbah).
takeaways: A separate Kaddish after Written Torah study and after Oral Torah study is not considered an unnecessary multiplication of Kaddishes.

paragraphs: Keshem sheasur laabor lipne hammitpallel kak asur laabor lipne haomer qaddish kemo shekkatab b"birke yosep" veayyen "minchat aharon" dap s" ammud g, mihu nireh im higgia haomer qaddish l"l yisrael" veyesh lazeh tzorek laabor lepanayv shari, veken anachnu nohagim:

clarification.explanation: Just as it is forbidden to pass in front of one who is praying, it is forbidden to pass in front of one saying Kaddish; but if the one saying Kaddish has reached 'Al Yisrael' and there is a need to pass, it is permitted.
takeaways: One should not pass in front of the one saying Kaddish, unless he has already reached 'Al Yisrael' and there is a need.

paragraphs: "yehe shemeh rabba mebarak" hu targum shel "yehi shemo haggadol meborak", laken yimshok millat "mebarek" im millat "rabba" veyomar "mebarek" habbe"t bqm"tz vehare"sh bepattach, sheaz perusho keillu meborak vekannizkar baacharonim, veyomar tay"v rishona shel tushbachta bchyr"q, gam kesheyyomar "lealam lealeme alemayya" yimshok millat "yitbarek" im millat "alemayya" shello yapsiq ben "alemayya" lemillat "yitbarek", veayyen magen abraham siman s"v seip qatan v"maamar mareddekay" siman n"v seip qatan v v"shalme tzibbur" dap p"d ammud d. gam yizzaher haoneh qaddish lehapsiq meat ben "amen" uben "yehe shemeh rabba" ki "amen" zeh qae addilel, umatchil hashshebach min "yehe shemeh", veyizzaher haoneh qaddish laanot bekol kocho rotzeh lomar bekol kavvanato, vegam yarim qolo meat, abal lo yarim yoter miqqol haomer qaddish, kedin haoneh amen sheeno rashshay lehagbihha qolo yoter min hambarek vekannizkar b"chesed lealpayim", vaaniyyat qaddish qodemet laaniyyat qedushsha im baim lashshomea beyachad, abal im kebar hitchil laanot qedushsha lo yapsiq laanot qaddish, veken im kebar shama qaddish echad veana, abal qedushsha adayin lo shama beoto hayyom debazeh aniyyat qedushsha qadim kede sheyyetze yede chobat qaddish uqedushsha vekannizkar b"chesed laalapim", veim shenayim omerim qaddish vezeh maqdim vezeh meacher yaaneh achar hammaqdim:

clarification.explanation: 'Yehei Shmei Rabba Mevarach' is the Aramaic translation of 'May His great Name be blessed' - one should connect 'Mevarach' with 'Rabba' (bet with kamatz, reish with patach), and likewise pronounce the first tav of 'Tushbechata' (later in the Kaddish) with a chirik; and when saying 'Le'alam Ul'almei Almaya,' one should connect the word 'Yitbarach' with 'Almaya' without pausing between them. The one answering Kaddish should pause slightly between 'Amen' and 'Yehei Shmei Rabba' (since that Amen belongs to what precedes it, and the praise begins from 'Yehei Shmei'), and should answer with all his strength (his intention), raising his voice slightly but not more than the one reciting. The response of Kaddish takes precedence over Kedushah if both come together; but if one has already begun answering Kedushah, one should not stop to answer Kaddish. And if one has already heard and answered one Kaddish that day and has not yet heard Kedushah, the response of Kedushah takes precedence, so as to fulfill the obligation of both Kaddish and Kedushah.
takeaways: Precise points of pronunciation in 'Yehei Shmei Rabba' and further in the Kaddish.
Kaddish takes precedence over Kedushah if they arrive together; but if one has already begun Kedushah, one does not stop.

paragraphs: Kepi dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l qaddish deqodem hodu veqodem yotzer, veshel achar haamida qodem ashre, veshel qodem tepilla ledavid, veshel qodem pittum haqqetoret, vekol chamishsha ellu choba hem veen haqqatan yukal leomeram lebaddo ella tzarik gadol lehotzi hatztzibbur yede chobatam, veqaddish sheqqodem "alenu leshabbeach" sheomerim achar "tanna debe eliyyahu" zeh niqra qaddish "yatom" shechakamenu za"l tiqqenu zeh leomero hayyetomim, veeno mikkelal chamishsha qaddishim hannizkarim shennitqenu letzorek haolamot, ella zeh haqqaddish hu baolam haasiyya sheyyesh toelet lanniptar im yomar oto beno tok shenem asar chodesh, vegam bekol yom yartzayt, veyesh bo shette toaliyyot haachat lehatztzilo middin gehinnam, vehashsheniyya lehakniso legan eden ulehaaloto mimmadrega lemadrega, lekak omerim oto hayyetomim tok shenem asar chodesh, vegam beyom yartzayt bekol shana veshana, vekak haya noheg rabbenu haari"y zy" lomar qaddish batera zeh bekol shana shenniptar bo abiv ben beshacharit ben bearbit vekannizkar beseper hakkavvanot ayyen sham, umatzati katub beseper "keter malkut" ketibat yad sheyyomar hayyatom belachash hen betok shenem asar chodesh hen beyom yartzayt bekol shana qodem qaddish zeh pesuqim mlp" byt" hammatchilim beotiyyot shem abiv o immo sheomer qaddish zeh baadam, ukeneged kol ot mishshemotam yomar pasuq echad davqa belachash veereb li tamo, veken rauy laasot demistabbera milleta veen bazeh hepsed:

clarification.explanation: According to the Arizal, five Kaddishes in the Shacharit prayer are obligatory (before 'Hodu,' before 'Yotzer,' after the Amidah before 'Ashrei,' before 'Tefillah LeDavid' [Psalm 86], before 'Pittum HaKetoret'), and only an adult (not a minor) may say them on behalf of the congregation, for the sake of rectifying the worlds. But the Kaddish before 'Aleinu LeShabeach' (after 'Tana DeVei Eliyahu') is called the 'Orphan's Kaddish' - instituted specifically for orphans, and is not among the five main Kaddishes; it has two benefits for the deceased: rescue from the judgment of Gehinnom, and elevation through the levels of Gan Eden. Therefore the orphan says it during the first twelve months and on every anniversary (yahrzeit).
takeaways: The five main Kaddishes of Shacharit - for the rectification of the worlds - are said specifically by an adult.
The Orphan's Kaddish (before Aleinu LeShabeach) is specifically for orphans, helping the deceased escape Gehinnom and ascend in Gan Eden.

paragraphs: Poh irenu y" nahagu lomar beqaddish batera zeh hen beshacharit hen bearbit "rabbanan bareku et Adonai hamborak", ak beir haqqodesh tibbaneh vetikkonen bimhera beyamenu lo nahagu lomar rabbanan, vehaqqehillot kol achat yaaseh keminhago bazeh, ubesipre haq' "rab pealim" asiti besiyyata dishmayya taam laamirat "rabbanan" hen kan, hen qodem birkat hattora baaliyyat seper tora:

clarification.explanation: In Baghdad the custom is to say in the Orphan's Kaddish (in Shacharit and Arvit) 'Rabbanan, bless the Lord who is blessed,' but in Jerusalem the custom is not to say 'Rabbanan'; each community follows its own custom.
takeaways: Saying 'Rabbanan Barchu' in the Orphan's Kaddish is the custom of Baghdad; Jerusalem does not follow this custom.

paragraphs: Katab haggaon chida" b"shiyyure beraka" siman sh"v seip qatan ch lepi mah shekkatab rabbenu haari"y ztz"l dehaqqaddish moil gam ken lehaalot nishmato nireh sheyyomar qaddish kol shenem asar chodesh, ella mippene hehamon yapchit shabua acharon kemo shekkatab harab "keneset haggedola" siman t"g dekevan dechashu shello yomru mishpat reshaim begehinnam shenem asar chodesh kol shemmechasser min shenem asar chodesh saggi ad kan leshono, upoh ayarenu bagdad nahagu bekak ubesiyyum achad asar chodesh osim limmud yoter veholekim al haqqeber veqorin yom zeh shana hachasera uposeqin achar zeh shabua echad bitchillat chodesh hashshanim asar vahagam deharab za"l katab deposeqin beshabua acharon shel chodesh achad asar, lo ikpat shezzeh hakkol shaveh, vekol zeh hu lipsoq min haqqaddishim sheomerim hayyetomim, abal qaddish sheachar hallimmud sheomer kol adam gam hem yomru: gam yesh minhag poh enenu sheim chal yom yartzayt beemtza hashshabua, matchilin hayyetomim lomar haqqaddishim millel shabbat haqqodem dehaynu mittepillat arbit shel shabbat ad sop mincha shel yom yartzayt veim chal yom yartzayt beyom shabbat matchilin maarabit shel shabbat haqqodem, veomerim kol hashshabua ad sop shabbat sheniyya shehu yom yartzayt, uminhag zeh huba b"shalme tzibbur" dap q"tz ammud b abal misseper hakkavvanot nireh lehedya shello haya rabbenu haari"y za"l omer qaddish al abiv ella raq beyom echad shel yartzayt ballayla ubayyom, veda ki mashmaut yartzayt hu yom happetira bilshon ashkenaz, vegam hasseparaddim hurgelu liqro oto beshem zeh besiprehem, veen bazeh rashe tebot o remez acher kemo shechoshebin haolam:

clarification.explanation: According to the Arizal, the Kaddish also helps elevate the soul of the deceased, and so it would be proper to say it for the full twelve months; but for the sake of the common people (so that it should not appear as though the deceased is judged as wicked in Gehinnom for a full year) they stop one week before the year's end. In Baghdad: they stop at the beginning of the twelfth month (a day called 'the incomplete year,' with additional study and a visit to the grave). Regarding a yahrzeit Kaddish that falls in the middle of the week, they begin saying it already from the Shabbat before. And this stopping applies only to the Kaddishes said by the orphans, but the Kaddish said after study - which every person says - continues to be said by them as well. And from Sefer HaKavanot it appears that the Arizal himself said Kaddish for his father only on the day of the yahrzeit itself, night and day. And 'yahrzeit' means 'day of passing' in the Ashkenazic language, and it is not an acronym or hint, as many people suppose.
takeaways: Orphan's Kaddishes for the deceased are said throughout the year minus one week (to avoid giving a negative impression).
Baghdad custom: begin saying the yahrzeit Kaddishes from the preceding Shabbat if the yahrzeit falls in the middle of the week.
The stopping applies only to the orphans' Kaddishes; the Kaddish said after study continues to be said.

paragraphs: Beinyan hanniptar belo zera o shebbeno qatan vesokerim echad sheyyomar baaburo qaddish nishalti besipri haq' "rab pealim" i mehanne bikhay gavna vekatabti besiyyata dishmayya sham ki ken matzati katub shehuba b"bet yosep" besop cheleq "yoreh dea" mashma shehaya lahem minhag qadmon liskor adam lomar qaddish bishbil nepesh hanniptar, veken mukach name mitteshubat mahari"y qulon za"l shoresh m"d yauy sham, veayyen seper "chayyim beyad" siman qy"d mah shekkatab taam leminhag ir veem beyisrael azzemir y" litten qaddish batera sheomerim qodem alenu leshabbeach leharab hammoreh shebbair ayyen sham, ubeseper "kisse eliyyahu" depus qarta qaddisha yerushalayim tibbaneh vetikkonen katab betiqqun shel taanit yabi acherim lehitannot immo ayyen sham, vekatabti sheal kol panim zeh haomer qaddish bead metim zarim mimmennu, yomar kol yom besop hayyom baqqasha zo "yehi ratzon millepaneka veku' shettachus vetachmol uterachem berob rachameka vachasadeka al nepesh rucha uneshama shel peloni ben pelonit, ulemaan haqqaddishim sheamarti ani abdeka hayyom hazzeh tebattel kol hamqatregim vehammastinim, veyaamdu melitze yosher lehamlitz tob al napsho rucho venishmato, vetilveh alehem hashshalom veyashebu bimnuchat shalom hashqet ubetach vetagbir chasadeka al middat haddin veyitmattequ haggeburot haqqashot al yede pele haelyon shehu chasadim gedolim verachamim gemurim yihyu leratzon vego'":

clarification.explanation: A deceased person without offspring, or whose son is a minor, for whom one hires a person to say Kaddish on his behalf - this is of avail, as is proven from ancient sources. One who says Kaddish for a deceased person who is a stranger to him should say, at the end of each day, a special request asking for mercy upon the soul of the deceased, that by virtue of the Kaddishes he said the accusers be nullified and there be peace and rest for his soul.
takeaways: Hiring a person to say Kaddish for a deceased person without a son is an ancient and effective custom.
One who says Kaddish for a stranger's deceased adds a personal request at day's end on behalf of his soul.

paragraphs: Besipre haq' "rab pealim" nishalti bearbaa o chamishsha sheomerim qaddish beyachad veechad mehem qolo namuk sheshshum echad min hatztzibbur eno shomea qolo i tzarik lememar qaddish im otam haomerim qaddish shehatztzibbur shomein qolam bilbad vehebeti sham dibre harab "emet leyaaqob" bemishpat habberakot laolin leseper tora dap k"d ot s gam hebeti dibre harab "binyan tziyyon" siman qk"b sheppiqpeq bazeh vehebeti od edut harab haggaon chasid mhr" minni nr"v beminhag hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz shehachazzan hu haomer et haqqaddish bekavvanot veim yesh echad min hatztzibbur sheyyesh lo yartzayt verotzeh lomar qaddish yomar belachash kede shello yearbeb hakkavvana shel hachazzan gam heid shebbeseper "petach haddebir" siman qk"h [eno matzuy etzlenu] gam ken katab dela ikpat bekak veim kol zeh haaleti dilkattechilla lo yaasu ken uminhag hachasidim hannizkar shane mishshum dela epshar belav haki: od nishalti sham baasara shellamedu tehillim verotzim kullam lomar qaddish sheen shum echad oneh vehebeti dibre harab "bene yeuddeh" ayash za"l siman g' veheerakti qetzat bazeh vehaaleti dilkattechilla yizzaharu lihyot echad oneh lahem haqqaddish:

clarification.explanation: Several people saying Kaddish together, one of whom has such a low voice that no one in the congregation hears him - the Ben Ish Chai concluded that ideally one should not act this way; and the custom of Beit El (that the chazan alone says it aloud with intention, and one with a yahrzeit says it quietly) is exceptional, since it is not otherwise possible there. Likewise, ten who studied Tehillim and all wish to say Kaddish without anyone answering - ideally, they should be careful that one person answers the Kaddish for them.
takeaways: Ideally, several people should not say Kaddish together when one's voice is inaudible to the congregation; the custom of Beit El (the chazan alone aloud, and the one with a yahrzeit quietly) is exceptional because there is no other way there. And with ten who studied Tehillim - they should be careful that one person answers for them.
